driver.c: wmain calls install_driver, then terminate_security_processes. CreateServiceW registers SERVICE_KERNEL_DRIVER with SERVICE_AUTO_START, then StartServiceW starts the returned service handle.
The service display name claims an NVIDIA filesystem filter; the file path is under System32/drivers. This claims identity but does not prove vendor provenance or driver vulnerability.

CreateFileW opens the Alinubx device. Toolhelp iterates processes and the equality test accepts only MsMpEng.exe and CSFalconService.exe. Their process IDs are passed by address to DeviceIoControl with 0x222024.

This targeted protected-security-process termination, with automatic kernel-driver startup, tips the judgement to MALICIOUS. No error checks or permissions bypass are implemented; administrative service-creation rights and a compatible existing driver are prerequisites. The driver image is absent, so successful loading, kernel exploitation and actual process death are unproved.
There is no download, network client, embedded driver, encryption or encoded second stage. C wide-string backslashes are ordinary source escaping, not obfuscation.
qualifier.py: Module import only defines schema/query/constants/functions; controlled execution with a stub boto3 module confirmed no calls at import time. No entry point, db-opening path or credential-acquisition routine exists.

Given a supplied record, aws_clients passes its key/secret/token to STS, Bedrock catalog and runtime clients. qualify_pair loops three regions, obtains caller identity, lists foundation models and inference profiles, and sends a ping/max_tokens=1 body to each enumerated model. Identity/model/profile tuples are returned locally; validate_inventory discards them.

SQL correlates access/secret/token records by source_url. The LEFT JOIN condition incorrectly filters token-less credential pairs out, because token.key_kind is filtered in WHERE after all records from that source have joined.

For a token-bearing pair, probing happens before the updater raises IndexError on pair[source_url]: the SELECT projects only three credential columns. A stubbed client plus a real in-memory SQLite database confirmed both defects; no status update or final commit occurs in that path.

BENIGN is the balance-of-evidence judgement for a credential-qualification module: supplied credentials, provider APIs, ordinary local SQL, no acquisition, unrelated export, concealment, deployment hook or shown unauthorized use. victim_domain is an unused schema column, not a runtime victim-selection operation. Ownership/authorization of the input inventory is unknown. Bugs and absent entry points limit effects but are not proof of benign intent.

All supported credential pairing, status SQL, explicit credential-client setup, STS requests, Bedrock discovery/inference and serialization findings remain. Inventory + API calls alone do not establish harvested credentials or compute hijacking.
job.plist: Parsed launchd job Label claims an Apple service; ProgramArguments points to an executable inside a user Library/com.apple.* directory and supplies --type=renderer. RunAtLoad=true requests launch when the job is loaded.

The conjunction of system-vendor identity, user-writable helper executable and renderer presentation tips the judgement to MALICIOUS. A bare Apple label is ordinary launchd configuration and does not alone establish masquerade.

The plist does not install or load itself, prove login activation, define a KeepAlive loop, download a stage, set environment injection or reveal helper behavior. SyncHelper bytes, installed LaunchAgents/Daemons location, signature and runtime history are missing.

Only two hostile composites are justified by these bytes. Every configured key is covered by structured-value findings; a third distinct hostile payload/network/collection behaviour cannot be established without the absent helper. No matcher limitation prevents coverage of any remaining supported operation.

correction_rationale: Moved provider/source/status schema evidence into database schema, state vocabulary into source-literal metadata, SQL pairing into database access, status SQL into row-write, and the explicit-credential Bedrock probe into AWS service capabilities. Suspicious severity was reduced to notable because these matchers require no unauthorized source, evasion or security-boundary bypass. These observations apply to legitimate secret inventories and credential health checks, including the supplied qualifier.

The hostile harvested-AWS workflow now additionally requires the existing provider-secret regex extraction finding. Its consumer for harvested Bedrock capacity remains hostile when that extraction evidence exists. The extracting-qualifier positive passes; the supplied-only qualifier does not. No attack technique was deleted.

Moved generic AWS parameter-field vocabulary out of environment and legacy source-syntax paths. Original case-insensitive matchers and every explicit consumer are preserved; descriptions no longer imply an environment read or shared-credentials file access.

Moved kernel-device control and compatible IOCTL clues from filesystem/impact into kernel-device capabilities, preserving matcher scope and consumers. A DeviceIoControl reference and a compatible number alone identify neither the target driver nor a hostile objective; that co-occurrence becomes notable. EDR-targeted killing stays hostile. PoisonX/DCRCV compatibility findings retain suspicious severity.

Moved bare Apple launchd labels into service configuration and the user-home executable location into filesystem paths. Helper-label severity becomes notable because the same label shape fits a system-service configuration. Relocated the actual user-Library Apple-service masquerade from the cache category into service identity. Renamed hidden-helper and LaunchAgent claims that exceeded the plist bytes; both original hostile composites remain.

Added one precise CreateServiceW automatic kernel-driver registration observation and one hostile persistence composite combining it with existing driver-backed EDR killing. The argument filters bind driver type and startup mode to the same API call; a separate SERVICE_AUTO_START mention and ordinary driver installation do not establish the hostile result.
consumer_audit: Exact references updated across rules and the pre-existing packed-table/IOCTL fixture contract. Archived historical reports were left as historical records.

Inspected ancestor selectors under credential-access, impact, launchd persistence, fs and fs/path/location. Removal of ordinary schema/parameter facts from credential-access intentionally prevents those facts alone supplying theft to MCP/webhook consumers. Actual extracting workflows retain the hostile credential-access finding.

Moving kernel-device control cannot empty fs/ or fs/file/ membership: that composite still requires retained filesystem device-path and DeviceIoControl observations. The added plist path cannot match the existing ELF/PE-specific filesystem-location consumers. The inspected PhantomPulse PE consumer cannot consume plist-only labels.
